advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a diagnostic (not a silent None) when an absolute script reference resolves to multiple `infra/**/<basename>` candidates in `_resolve_repo_script`.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:123: `        return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`

The gate exists precisely to catch deploy-relevant scripts omitted from *_PATHS; a basename collision makes the ENTRYPOINT/install reference INVISIBLE to derivation — the check produces the same 'nothing' whether the path is covered or was never derived (fail-open).
ABSENCE: no diagnostic is emitted for the len(matches) > 1 case; it is silently skipped rather than flagged.
advisory.finding: `_resolve_repo_script` silently drops any absolute (container-installed) script reference whose basename collides with another file under `infra/` — `return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None` treats a >1 match as unresolvable and yields None, so the reference is never derived and its manifest omission goes undetected.
scenarios: A future infra change adds a second `mcp-entrypoint.sh` (or similarly-named script) elsewhere under infra/, so the Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT reference no longer resolves and its drift class stops being guarded.
advisory.suggested_fix: When len(matches) > 1, surface it as a diagnostic (ambiguous resolution) rather than returning None so the collision is visible instead of dropping the reference.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runtime floor assertion in `check()`/`derive_paths` that the known recurrence-class paths (or a nonzero minimum) were actually derived, so a parsing regression fails loud instead of passing blind.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:227: `    return diagnostics` — empty when derived is empty OR when all derived paths are covered
scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:187: `    for dockerfile in sorted(compose_dir.glob("Dockerfile.*")):` — a Dockerfile renamed off this glob simply yields fewer derived paths, no error

ABSENCE: derive_paths / check contain no assertion that a minimum known set (the historically-drifted recurrence classes) was actually derived; only the unit test pins that against the current tree, not the runtime gate.
advisory.finding: The derivation has no liveness/floor assertion: `check()` returns clean both when every derived path is covered AND when the Dockerfile/compose parsing silently derived fewer (or zero) paths (e.g. a Dockerfile renamed off the `Dockerfile.*` glob, a compose directive moved to multi-line YAML list form, or a directive-syntax change). The producer emitting nothing is indistinguishable from a passing check.
scenarios: An infra refactor changes Dockerfile naming or moves a compose entrypoint to YAML block-list form; parsing silently matches nothing and the gate reports GREEN while blind to all future drift.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert a nonempty derived set and that a small hardcoded anchor set (e.g. mcp-entrypoint.sh, compose-up.sh) is present in `derive_paths` output; emit a diagnostic if the producer went empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle YAML block-list `entrypoint:`/`command:` forms in `_derive_from_compose`, or document/assert that only inline form is supported.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:161: `        for raw in _iter_sh_tokens(stripped.split(":", 1)[1]):` — only reads tokens on the same line as the key

docker-compose.yml uses list-form for `test:`/`command`-like directives elsewhere (e.g. healthcheck `test: ["CMD", ...]`), so block-list entrypoint syntax is a realistic future form that would be missed.
advisory.finding: `_derive_from_compose` only matches single-line `entrypoint:`/`command:` values via `re.match(r"^(entrypoint|command):", stripped)`, so a YAML block-list form (`entrypoint:` on its own line followed by `- script.sh` items) is silently not derived — another way the derivation can under-produce without any signal.
scenarios: A service later declares `entrypoint:` in YAML block-list form pointing at an infra .sh script; the reference is silently not derived and its manifest coverage goes unchecked.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives check() (via monkeypatching gate.EXCLUSIONS) with a reason-less entry and a nonexistent-file entry, asserting the corresponding 'carries no reason' and 'names no repo file (stale)' diagnostics are emitted.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:215-218 add `diagnostics.append(f"EXCLUSION {path} carries no reason")` and `diagnostics.append(f"EXCLUSION {path} names no repo file (stale — remove or fix it)")`

tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py:116-120 only asserts the real EXCLUSIONS satisfy the invariant (`reason.strip()`, `(_REPO_ROOT / path).is_file()`) — it does not invoke check() with a bad exclusion

Named violating inputs never tested: EXCLUSIONS={'infra/scripts/nonexistent.sh': 'reason'} must yield a 'names no repo file (stale)' diagnostic; EXCLUSIONS={'<real file>': ''} must yield a 'carries no reason' diagnostic
ABSENCE rationale: check() cannot take repo_root-scoped EXCLUSIONS as a parameter (EXCLUSIONS is module-global) so the diagnostic branch is exercisable only via monkeypatch, and no test does so
advisory.finding: The stale-exclusion diagnostic path in check() (the diff's declared 'a stale exclusion is itself flagged' contract) is never driven: no test feeds check()/uncovered a malformed EXCLUSIONS to confirm the 'carries no reason' and 'names no repo file (stale)' diagnostics actually fire. test_every_exclusion_carries_a_reason_and_names_a_real_file merely re-asserts the current real EXCLUSIONS are valid using the same predicate the production code applies, so a regression that breaks the diagnostic emission (e.g. dropping the reason/is_file checks) would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches gate.EXCLUSIONS to {'infra/scripts/does-not-exist.sh': 'x'} and asserts any('names no repo file' in d for d in gate.check(_REPO_ROOT)); and a second with {'<a real derived path>': ''} asserting a 'carries no reason' diagnostic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add direct unit tests for _resolve_repo_script covering the /app/ prefix branch and the absolute-path basename resolution including the multi-match ambiguity guard.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:111-123 add the `_BUILD_CONTEXT_PREFIX` strip branch and the absolute-path `matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None` ambiguity guard
tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py has no test naming _resolve_repo_script; only derive_paths against the real repo touches it indirectly
ABSENCE rationale: no test drives _resolve_repo_script with a '/app/foo.sh' input or an absolute path whose basename is ambiguous
advisory.finding: _resolve_repo_script's added resolution branches — the `/app/` build-context prefix strip and the container-absolute-path basename-glob resolution with its `len(matches) == 1` ambiguity guard — have no direct test; they are exercised only incidentally through the real-repo derivation, so the ambiguity guard (returning None when a basename matches multiple infra files) and the /app/ mapping are not pinned against regression.
